terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; comparative facilior, superlative facillimus
evidence: Caes. BG 1.6.2: iter multō facilius atque expedītius (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “It’s easy to …” is facile est with an infinitive. The adverb is facile, easily, and most easily facillimē (Cic. Sen. 7). The opposite is difficilis (see difficult).

phrases.latin: Haec dum incipiās gravia sunt, dumque ignōrēs: ubi cognōris, facilia.
phrases.english: These things are hard while you are starting and don’t know them; once you know them, they are easy.

phrases.latin: ‘facilia’ inquit ‘mē docē’. cui praeceptor ‘ista’ inquit ‘omnibus eadem sunt, aequē difficilia’
phrases.english: ‘Teach me the easy things,’ he said; and his teacher said, ‘These are the same for everyone, and just as hard.’

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius, loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
